Hi Tom / Ava —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size the Dedicated pool for your POC properly (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private was discussed — looks like Dedicated is the likely path for the POC given data residency + predictable throughput needs).

Recap (from our side):
- POC goal: embed assistive clinical summarization inside provider workflow (HIPAA scope).
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 400ms for 1–2 user flows, non-blocking background jobs can be slower.
- Expected traffic pattern (your estimate): 1k daily active providers, peak 09:00–11:00 with burstiness.
- Security: Private VPC considered for later phase; POC prefers Redwood Dedicated with encrypted volumes and SOC2 controls.

Clarifying asks (helps Ben/Neha run the capacity workbook):
1) Can you confirm peak RPS/TPS during the busiest hour (not daily totals)?
2) Average prompt length and average generated tokens per request (or a small sample of calls)?
3) How many concurrent interactive requests do you expect at peak (users making requests at same time)?
4) Are there any long-running chain calls (tooling / function calls) that require keeping KV cache warm for >30s?

I attached a quick capacity workbook template — if you can fill the highlighted cells, Ben will convert into GPU sku targets (H100 vs A100 vs A10G tradeoffs) and concurrency guidance.

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. Filling in answers inline below and attaching a CSV export of a representative day from our telemetry (sanitized). Hope this helps.

Answers:
1) Peak TPS (our terminology is RPS): during the busiest hour we see sustained 20 RPS and micro-bursts up to ~45 RPS for 2–3 minutes when multiple providers batch-sign notes.
2) Prompt/response token mix: average prompt ~180 tokens (patient context + instructions); average generation ~720 tokens. We have a small subset (10% of calls) with much longer responses (~1.5k tokens) for full discharge summaries.
3) Concurrent interactive at peak: ~65 concurrent interactive requests (many reads, then submit generation).
4) KV cache / long-lived contexts: yes — for some users we keep a 2–3 turn context live; cache warm periods ~60s for a subset of sessions.

Attached: daily_telemetry_sample.csv and a short doc with latency targets. We prefer Dedicated for POC because of the predictable perf + encryption. We are open to a small Private VPC for Phase 2.

Hi Tom — appreciate the telemetry export, that’s exactly what we need. Quick technical thoughts based on your numbers (20 RPS sustained, spikes to 45 RPS, avg prompt 180 / gen 720 tokens, 10% long 1.5k tokens, ~65 concurrent interactions):

- GPU choices:
  - H100 (best perf for long-context / high throughput) — fewer GPUs but higher cost; great if you want headroom for 1.5k-token responses at low p95 latency.
  - A100 40GB (balanced) — good middle ground; easier availability in Dedicated pools.
  - A10G / L4-style (cost-efficient) — ok if you can accept slightly higher p95 for long responses and use aggressive batching + caching.

- Initial sizing heuristic:
  - If p95 target 400ms for ~900 token gen: estimate ~10–12 token/ms on A100-class kernels (very workload dependent). Using rough math: 900 tokens / (10 tokens/ms) = 90ms per request on pure generation time — but overhead, batching inefficiencies, and KV cache means ~150–250ms. For 20 sustained RPS we need concurrency headroom ~20–30 concurrent generator contexts; spikes to 45 RPS recommend 2–3x burst capacity or autoscale.

- Practical recommendation for POC:
  Option A (balanced): 4x A100-40GB Dedicated GPUs with continuous batching + prefix caching. Expect to comfortably hit p95 ~350–450ms for the 900-token median, with autoscale to handle bursts.
  Option B (latency-first): 2x H100s (larger instances) + reserved burst capacity for spikes; fewer instances but higher cost.
  Option C (cost-first): 6x A10G (smaller GPUs) with aggressive batching and larger batch windows for non-interactive flows; expect higher p95 on worst-case long summaries.

- Concurrency / batching: we recommend setting target concurrency per GPU at 20–30 generator contexts for A100; the platform can maintain KV-cache warm across contexts for your 60s sessions which will reduce upstream token work for short-turn interactions.

Next technical steps:
- Ben/Neha to run a quick simulation with the CSV, produce a recommended SKU mix and expected p95/cost (in the attached workbook).
- Book a 30–45m sizing workshop with your infra lead and security if possible — propose Mon/Tue next week.

I’m attaching a sample latency report from a similar POC so you can see end-to-end numbers.
